ELI5 How do vinyl records work?

Records are pieces of plastic/vinyl with lots of grooves (tiny tracks that generally spiral around from the outside of the record towards the middle. In each track/groove there are bumps in the record for recorded elements. A needle is used to both stay inside of the groove channel/track, and to lightly graze over the record's bumps. Grazing past the bumps causes the record needle to vibrate. The vibrations are tiny (microscopic), but are able to be amplified to be loud and audible. This is all done at usually 33 revolutions per minute or a faster 45 revolutions per minute.

also, the bumps are mostly horizontal, like a waveform - this was/is done for recordings on a single channel. Stereo recordings actually use a similar principle where the groove displaces the needle at 45 deg angles left and right - a combination of horizontal and vertical movement. more on this HERE

I don't like the term right-libertrianism. I was as left wing as they come, we are talking reading Chomsky and the like. Then I learned economics, and discovered the non-aggression principle and began to really understand that rights are not given to us by government but instead governments are created to secure natural rights from tyranny before they all too often become tyrants themselves. Now I am a so-called "right libertarian" but I don't like the implied connection to the republicans who are just as foul as the left wingers just on different issues. The right to bear arms is not more or less important than the right to marry whomever you wish. The drug war is not more unjust than the war on immigration. The right and left sides aren't opposites, they are complements.
Today's right and left act merely as teams to hide obscene prejudices and ignorance behind.

I find the it more useful to split libertarians into descriptive libertarians and prescriptive libertarians.

Descriptive libertarians say that in the absence of government market methods for protection of property would arise. Such a society would largely be libertarian-minded as forcing your own preferences on others is expensive if they have to pay out of their own pocket to do it. Services such as courts, police, firefighting, national defense and healthcare would be provided by the market with more accountability at lower cost.

The prescriptive libertarian starts with how he thinks things ought to be. They will start with an end in mind, such as the non-aggression principle or protection of one's rights. They will try to find a way for such rights to be defended in the libertarian framework.

I think the only two groups of libertarianism are really anarchists and minarchists. Right and left have no meaning in libertarianism. It just happens to be that in our current climate the republicans have a small libertarian movement (ron paul, rand paul, justin amash, thomas massie and others) whereas the democrats have no semblance whatsoever of anybody who believes in liberty.
